title: Gate A at merge reads the persisted triage verdict, never the caller

story.i_want_to: the merge precondition to judge Gate A from the triage verdict loopctl persisted
story.so_that: the principal driving a merge cannot also certify the triage it depends on

rationale: Every merge-precondition verdict is stamped gate_a_inputs: caller_asserted: the trio's outputs come from the request, so whoever drives the merge also supplies the triage it is judged against. The triage verdict is persisted per dispatch, before any implementation exists, but as one merged verdict that hides the disagreement Gate A exists to see. Carrying the three lens verdicts in that persisted payload and reading them server-side removes the merge caller from the decision; the lens verdicts are still runner-authored, but by an earlier, separate session.

acceptance_criteria.description: The triage_verdict message accepts optional lens_verdicts naming each of analyst, architect and engineer exactly once, only beside a verdict and within RunnerLensVerdict.max_bytes/0; any other shape is refused invalid_payload and records nothing.

MergePrecondition decides Gate A from triage_verdicts.lens_verdicts of the story's most recent triage verdict, translated by GateAInput to GateA's output shape, and the verdict carries gate_a_inputs: :persisted_triage.

A {escalated, queued, :human_resolution} transition that resolves an escalation taken over :triage_escalate, or over :merge_gate with a Gate A reason, and is recorded after that triage verdict, satisfies Gate A with gate_a_inputs: :human_resolution.
A human resolution of any other escalation (for example :attempts_exhausted or a Gate B-only :merge_gate) does not satisfy Gate A.
A story with no persisted lens verdicts and no qualifying human resolution gets a refuse decision naming gate_a_inputs_missing, with no retry_after.
A request carrying trio_outputs is accepted, the field is ignored, the verdict records trio_outputs_ignored: true, and the OpenAPI spec no longer lists trio_outputs as required.

An MCP tool merge_precondition calls POST /api/v1/stories/:id/merge-precondition, its description names the refusals and the key it needs, and route_coverage.test.js no longer declares the route a gap.
Evaluating a tenant A story never reads a tenant B triage verdict.

technical_notes: Contract: lens_verdicts on RunnerTriageVerdictMessage in priv/runner_contract/v1.json, x-contract-version 1.15.0; runner_contract_test.exs binds both directions
Storage: the message's lens_verdicts are on the envelope, not in the verdict payload, so they get their own jsonb column triage_verdicts.lens_verdicts, keyed by lens (migration 20260923120000)

Gate A input was lib/loopctl/delivery/merge_precondition.ex:277 (caller_asserted); GateA.evaluate/1 requires three outputs in its own vocabulary (verdict, numeric confidence), so Loopctl.Delivery.GateAInput translates the wire's outcome and confidence enum
Order the resolution against the verdict with story_stage_events, which record the edge and the escalation it resolved, not by comparing timestamps across tables
Controller spec: lib/loopctl_web/controllers/merge_precondition_controller.ex:208; MCP tool is a lib module plus an index.js case plus a README row
non_goals: Does not run the gates at triage (US-44.2)
Does not change Gate B or the hard diff bound
Does not reuse the verdict payload for lens verdicts: they share no byte budget with the verdict
